12522.name: Cam Ward
12522.headline: 0-5 Titans offense sputtering; Ward's sophomore year is stalling
12522.news: Ward went 23-of-36 for 170 yards, no touchdowns and an interception in the 26-3 Week 5 loss to Houston (Oct. 11), taking a season-high four sacks as Tennessee managed 187 total yards. Through five games he has roughly 896 passing yards with a 3:3 TD:INT ratio and a ~63% completion rate. Head coach Robert Saleh said he has not considered a QB change, and OC Brian Daboll has publicly backed him, though media are openly debating a benching (Mitchell Trubisky is the backup). Local film reviews spread the blame across the offensive line, a thin supporting cast and Daboll's red-zone play-calling.
12522.take: In superflex, Ward still holds value simply as a young starting QB with a long runway, but his 2026 production is unstartable and his value is cratering in real time. The context (bad line, new playcaller, rookie WR Carnell Tate still developing) explains some of it, which is why selling for pennies right now is a mistake. For a rebuilding team, he is a reasonable hold-and-hope stash: the downside risk is a benching or a 2027 QB pick, so do not buy aggressively either. Re-evaluate after the trade deadline window based on whether Tennessee shows any signs of progress.

6797.name: Justin Herbert
6797.headline: Herbert turnover-prone behind rookie-laden line as Chargers fall to 0-5
6797.news: In the 23-17 Week 5 loss to Denver (Oct. 11), Herbert completed 14 of 24 for 121 yards, a TD and an INT, ran six times for 54 yards and fumbled twice (one lost) while being sacked five times; WR Quentin Johnston was inactive (chest). Season totals sit around 937 yards, 5 TD and 7 INT on a 59% completion rate with 17 sacks taken. PFF grades him 35th of 36 qualifying QBs, and the Chargers started four rookies on the offensive line. Some reports reference a new offensive coordinator, but that detail is not consistently confirmed across sources.
6797.take: This is the worst stretch of Herbert's career, and it is mostly an environment problem: a rookie offensive line and missing pass catchers. He is still 28 with a long track record of top-tier play, so in superflex his long-term value is far higher than his current production suggests. For a 1-4 rebuilding team, he is the kind of veteran QB contenders still pay for, but selling at the bottom of his value would be poor timing. Hold, and only move him if a contender offers near his pre-season price.

12533.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
12533.headline: Efficient but capped: 'Bill' leads carries, Rachaad White leads snaps
12533.news: In the 27-27 Week 5 tie with the Giants (Oct. 11), Croskey-Merritt ran 11 times for 82 yards including a 33-yard TD on the opening drive, but did not get a carry over the final 14-plus minutes of regulation or overtime. Usage reports show him at roughly a 35% snap share and 16% route share, with Rachaad White out-snapping him 37 to 22 and handling passing downs. Earlier in the season he dipped to nine carries for 15 yards in Week 4. Kaytron Allen, Jerome Ford and recently re-signed Austin Ekeler round out a crowded room.

That makes him a touchdown-dependent RB3/flex in half PPR. In dynasty he is a cheap second-year back with proven efficiency; the team pushed him to become an every-down player in the offseason, and so far that has not happened. Hold rather than sell low; he could become a buy if White or Washington's coaching staff changes.

13269.name: Fernando Mendoza
13269.headline: No. 1 pick debuts in mop-up duty; Cousins keeps the job for now
13269.news: Mendoza got his first regular-season snaps in Week 5 (Oct. 11), replacing Kirk Cousins with about six minutes left in a 45-17 loss at New England and going 6-of-8 for 48 yards. 13269.take: The rookie hasn't started yet, so for now his value is all about the future. Two straight losses and a blowout cameo make a mid-season switch more likely than it was in September, but nobody has reported a date, and preseason predictions of a Week 6 takeover were only guesses. In a 10-team superflex dynasty league, a No. 1 overall QB with a likely starting job in 2027 has real value for a rebuilding team. He also had a pick-six and some sloppy moments in the preseason, so don't pay a premium as if he's already proven. The best time to buy is now, while managers trying to win this year see him as dead roster space.

12527.headline: Banged-up Jeanty grinding at 3.4 YPC; receiving work keeps him afloat

A possible switch to rookie QB Mendoza could make the offense worse in the short term. In dynasty he's still a young bell-cow profile worth holding, so don't sell him for less than he's worth. For Weekend Warriors, only buy him at a discount from a frustrated manager. Don't pay RB1 prices for a player putting up RB2 numbers at less than full health.

In dynasty he is a 2025 first-round pick with a growing role, which is the profile a rebuilding team should hold, and his price may be low enough to buy.

9997.name: Zay Flowers
9997.headline: Playing through a foot injury and still Baltimore's top target

With Jackson back he should return to the big-play production he showed early in the season. He is a weekly WR2 in redraft, with a little extra caution because of the foot. In dynasty he is young and on a long-term deal, so he has value whether you are rebuilding or not. Hold him unless a contender pays a premium.

6770.name: Joe Burrow
6770.headline: Four-TD day in Miami heads into Bengals' Week 6 bye
6770.news: In the Bengals' 31-24 win at Miami on Oct. 11, Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for only 190 yards but threw four touchdowns and no interceptions. The scores went to four different players: Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Ja'Marr Chase, whose TD covered 45 yards. 6770.take: Burrow is healthy and producing like a top-10 QB. He has thrown as many as 54 passes in a game and still has Chase as his top target. In dynasty superflex he is still a core QB in his prime, but you're 1-4 and rebuilding, so his value to you is in what he could bring back. If a contender pays a premium (a 2027 1st plus a young asset), selling makes sense. Don't dump him cheaply, though, because elite superflex QBs hold their value for years.

11584.name: Bucky Irving
11584.headline: 165-yard eruption vs. Dallas, but Gainwell still eats snaps
11584.news: On Thursday, Oct. 8, Irving ran 21 times for a career-high 165 yards in the Bucs' 24-16 win at Dallas, the team's first win after an 0-4 start. He broke a 72-yard run to open the second half, scored twice, and caught 2 passes for 10 yards. No other Tampa back topped five carries. Snap data still show a split: Irving has played roughly 55-60% of snaps, Kenneth Gainwell around 40%, and Sean Tucker and Gainwell have taken some red-zone work. Pittsburgh is the Week 6 opponent.
11584.take: That box score came against Dallas, which has allowed the most rushing yards in the league (about 168 per game), so don't treat it as his new baseline. Irving is the clear lead runner, but Gainwell takes passing-down and some goal-line work. That limits his ceiling more than his 2024 rookie profile suggested, and Tampa's offense with rookie QB Jalon Daniels is not a scoring machine. In redraft he is a solid RB2 starter. In dynasty he's 24 and productive, but the shoulder history and split role argue against paying peak price after a spike week. If someone values him as an RB1 off this game, a rebuilding team should listen.

8138.name: James Cook
8138.headline: Two TDs vs. Rams, but fumbles are opening door for Davis
8138.news: In Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday, Oct. 12, Cook ran 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for 7 yards. He also fumbled twice and lost one on the Bills' first overtime possession, which nearly decided the game. That makes four fumbles in five games. On the season he has 532 rushing yards and five TDs. Ray Davis played a season-high number of snaps in that game, and SI's Bills site suggested a more even split could follow. Week 6 is at Las Vegas.
8138.take: Cook is a top-12 back in redraft thanks to his volume and Buffalo's scoring offense. Start him at the Raiders without hesitation. The fumbles are the real risk: Davis has already taken some of his snaps, and if Cook drops it again, a more even timeshare could cut into his ceiling. He is 27, so in dynasty this is about the peak of his value. For a 1-4 rebuilding team, selling him to a contender for picks or younger players is the smart move while his touchdown numbers look this good.

12512.name: Quinshon Judkins
12512.headline: Day-to-day ankle 'tweak'; not ruled out vs. Baltimore
12512.news: Judkins was seen in a walking boot after the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets. A day-to-day ankle on a previously repaired joint, plus a tough Baltimore matchup, makes him a risky Week 6 play even if active; check Friday's report and the inactives. In dynasty he is a young three-down-capable back on a rookie deal, which is what a rebuild wants, so hold. Keep an eye on whether this lingers, since a recurring issue in the same ankle would hurt his long-term outlook.

8131.headline: 11 catches, two TDs; now a top-five TE play

8144.headline: Quiet Week 5, but still among the league's yardage leaders

He also has a concussion history. In dynasty he's a hold, and you can sell only if a contender pays a true WR1 price.

12469.name: Dylan Sampson
12469.headline: IR window may open as Browns backfield thins out
12469.news: Cleveland put Sampson on IR in mid-September with a knee injury, and he has missed four games. Todd Monken said on Oct 12 that the team might open his 21-day practice window this week. Lead back Quinshon Judkins is day-to-day after tweaking his ankle in the Week 5 loss to the Jets. Raheim Sanders (hip) is reportedly headed to IR, which would leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the only other healthy back. Opening the window would not guarantee that Sampson is activated for Sunday's game against Baltimore.
12469.take: Sampson's value is all about opportunity. Judkins is banged up and Sanders is likely out, so the Browns could need him quickly once he is healthy. He was a 2025 fourth-round pick out of Tennessee, and his role projects as a change-of-pace and passing-down back behind Judkins rather than a lead back. In redraft, he is a reasonable bench stash in deeper leagues, especially for Judkins managers, but don't start him until he is activated and you see his snap share. In dynasty he is a cheap backup with some contingent value, so hold him rather than pay up.

In dynasty he is a recent first-round pick with a hamstring-shortened ramp-up, so a slow rookie start is not a reason to sell. Holding, or buying quietly at a discount, makes sense.
